trust-in-government.name: Trust in government
trust-in-government.line: I don't trust the government to do what's right.

sources.passage: Just 17% of Americans now say they trust the government in Washington to do what is right “just about always” (2%) or “most of the time” (15%).
44% of respondents now have low or no trust in their national government

trust-in-government.prevalence: Just 17% of Americans trust the government in Washington to do what is right just about always or most of the time (Pew). Across OECD countries, 44% have low or no trust in their national government. "The government/Poor leadership" is the most-named problem in Gallup's open-ended question, at 26%.

fair-elections.name: Fair elections
fair-elections.line: I'm not sure our elections are fair and honest.

sources.passage: Forty-nine percent are confident in electoral honesty, while 51% are not.

fair-elections.prevalence: Forty-nine percent of Americans are confident in the honesty of elections and 51% are not (Gallup World Poll).

political-violence.name: Political violence
political-violence.line: I worry that anger over politics is turning into violence.

sources.passage: About three-quarters of poll respondents see it as a significant issue, an increase of 4 points from July, before Kirk’s death.
Nearly a third of Americans – 30% – say people may have to resort to violence in order to get the country back on track
Rise of extremism 9% (full list, % mentioned in May 2026, global country average)

political-violence.prevalence: About three-quarters of Americans see political violence as a significant issue, and 30% say people may have to resort to violence to get the country back on track (NPR/PBS News/Marist). Rise of extremism is a top worry for 9% on average across Ipsos's countries.

government-surveillance.name: Government surveillance
government-surveillance.line: I worry the government is watching what I do and say.

sources.passage: About seven-in-ten U.S. adults (71%) say they are very or somewhat concerned about this, up from 64% in 2019.

government-surveillance.prevalence: About seven in ten U.S. adults (71%) are very or somewhat concerned about how the government uses the data it collects about them, up from 64% in 2019 (Pew).

benefits-red-tape.name: Red tape
benefits-red-tape.line: I see people lose help they qualify for because of paperwork.

sources.passage: Across all states with available data, 69% of all people disenrolled had their coverage terminated for procedural reasons.
at least 25,198,000 Medicaid enrollees had been disenrolled during the unwinding

leads: Founder pool (hierarchy v2), paperwork_bureaucracy: "benefits i depend on have been denied reduced or terminated", "i can t figure out how to apply for or keep benefits i need".
benefits-red-tape.prevalence: At least 25,198,000 Medicaid enrollees were disenrolled during the unwinding, and 69% of them lost coverage for procedural reasons rather than being found ineligible (KFF).

shutdowns.name: Shutdowns
shutdowns.line: I see paychecks and food aid stop when the government shuts down.

sources.passage: It’s a 1,680% increase from the number of calls 211 received last year. ... benefits from the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program weren’t delivered to about 275,000 West Virginia residents.

shutdowns.prevalence: When food benefits weren't delivered to about 275,000 West Virginia residents during the shutdown, calls to 211 rose 1,680% over the year before.
